title: A disjoint union of smooth schemes over a base is smooth
statement: Let $S$ be a scheme, $n\ge1$, and $f_i:Y_i\to S$ ($i=1,\dots,n$) smooth morphisms of schemes [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms]. Then the induced morphism $(f_1,\dots,f_n):Y_1\amalg\cdots\amalg Y_n\to S$ from the disjoint union (coproduct) of the $Y_i$ is smooth.

source.place: Morphisms, Definition (definition-smooth), tag 01V5: $f$ is smooth if it is smooth at every point $x$, a condition on an affine open neighbourhood of $x$ (so local on the source); each $Y_i$ is an open subscheme of the disjoint union, and the restriction of $(f_1,\dots,f_n)$ to it is $f_i$. The identification with [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms] is Stacks 02H6 as recorded there
